answer: Stake-weighted influence caps resist sybils: an identity's voting or earning weight is bounded by the collateral it has locked, not by how many accounts it holds. Splitting one stake across a swarm is a fable of free power — the total influence just ripples back to what that single pool of capital could ever buy. A honest whale and a thousand fakes funded from one meadow of money command the same ceiling, so fragmenting identity gains nothing.
